arxiv-2102-02944.title: Atomtronic protocol designs for NOON states
arxiv-2102-02944.creator: Daniel S. Grün, Karin Wittmann W, Leandro H. Ymai, Jon Links & Angela Foerster
arxiv-2102-02944.description: Abstract The ability to reliably prepare non-classical states will play a major role in the realization of quantum technology. NOON states, belonging to the class of Schrödinger cat states, have emerged as a leading candidate for several applications. Starting from a model of dipolar bosons confined to a closed circuit of four sites, we show how to generate NOON states.

arxiv-2105-08866.title: Localization, Convexity, and Star Aggregation
arxiv-2105-08866.creator: Suhas Vijaykumar
arxiv-2105-08866.description: Abstract Offset Rademacher complexities have been shown to provide tight upper bounds for the square loss in a broad class of problems including improper statistical learning and online learning. We show that the offset complexity can be generalized to any loss that satisfies a certain general convexity condition.

arxiv-2311-01572.title: Sign-problem-free effective models of triangular lattice quantum antiferromagnets
arxiv-2311-01572.creator: Henry Shackleton, Subir Sachdev
arxiv-2311-01572.description: Abstract The triangular lattice antiferromagnet with S = 1 / 2 S=1/2 spins and nearest neighbor interactions is known to have long-range antiferromagnetic order, with nearest-neighbor spins at an angle of 120 degrees. Numerical studies of quantum phases proximate to this state have been limited to small systems because the of the sign-problem in Monte Carlo simulations in imaginary time.

arxiv-2311-09143.title: Experimental Study of Condensation of Water on Polydimethylsiloxane-Coated Copper Surfaces Volume: Volume x, Issue x, 2023August 9, 2026
arxiv-2311-09143.creator: Shuai Li, Michael Kappl, Hans-Jürgen Butt, Peter Stephan, Tatiana Gambaryan-Roisman
arxiv-2311-09143.description: Abstract Modification of surfaces to enable dropwise condensation is a promising approach for achieving high condensation rates. In this work, we present an experimental study on condensation of water on copper surfaces coated with an ultrathin, 5 nm − 10 nm $5\text{\,}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{m}$-$10\text{\,}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{m}$ thick polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer.

arxiv-2407-11885.title: On collectively almost (limitedly, order) L-weakly compact sets of operators
arxiv-2407-11885.creator: Safak Alpay, Eduard Emelyanov, Svetlana Gorokhova
arxiv-2407-11885.description: Abstract We prove collective versions of semi-duality theorems for sets of almost (limitedly, and order) L-weakly compact operators. Keywords: L-weakly compact set, Banach lattice, domination problem MSC 2020: 46B50, 47B01, 47B07, 47B65 1 Introduction and Preliminaries The theory of L-weakly compact operators goes back to P. Meyer-Nieberg.

arxiv-2408-09960.title: Causality-Inspired Models for Financial Time Series Forecasting
arxiv-2408-09960.creator: Daniel Cunha Oliveira, Yutong Lu, Xi Lin, Mihai Cucuringu, André Fujita
arxiv-2408-09960.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel Cunha Oliveira, Yutong Lu, Xi Lin, Mihai Cucuringu, André Fujita. We introduce a novel framework to financial time series forecasting that leverages causality-inspired models to balance the trade-off between invariance to distributional changes and minimization of prediction errors. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to conduct a comprehensive comparative analysis among state-of-the-art causal discovery algorithms, benchmarked against non-causal feature selection techniques, in the application of forecasting asset returns.

arxiv-2412-00269.title: Examining a Quantum System Subject to Energy Decoherence
arxiv-2412-00269.creator: Henry Crumley
arxiv-2412-00269.description: Abstract This paper studies the energy decoherence of an interacting quantum system. It first reviews the experiments that motivated the postulates of quantum mechanics. It then discusses a decoherence that occurs dynamically in a closed system. This effect is studied in interacting quantum systems consisting of an oscillator and spins using analytical and numerical methods.

arxiv-2508-01558.title: EvoVLMA: Evolutionary Vision-Language Model Adaptation Conference: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 27–31, 2025; Dublin, Ireland Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’25), October 27–31, 2025, Dublin, Ireland DOI: 10.1145/3
arxiv-2508-01558.creator: Kun Ding, Ying Wang, Shiming Xiang
arxiv-2508-01558.description: Abstract . Pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have been exploited in various Computer Vision tasks (e.g., few-shot recognition) via model adaptation, such as prompt tuning and adapters. However, existing adaptation methods are designed by human experts, requiring significant time cost and experience.

arxiv-2510-20574.title: After 54 years of bar instability studies: a fresh surprise
arxiv-2510-20574.creator: J. A. Sellwood, Victor P. Debattista, R. G. Carlberg
arxiv-2510-20574.description: Abstract The well-known bar instability of rotationally-supported disk galaxy models has been studied extensively since its first discovery over mvhalf a century ago. We were therefore very surprised to find cases of disks embedded in rigid halos, which on the basis of widely-cited criteria should be unstable, that appeared to be robustly stable.

arxiv-2601-11214.title: T ⋆ : Progressive Block Scaling for MDM Through Trajectory Aware RL
arxiv-2601-11214.creator: Hanchen Xia †⋆ , Baoyou Chen †⋆ , Yutang Ge ‡ , Guojiang Zhao § , Siyu Zhu †♢ † Shanghai Academy of AI for Science, ‡ School of Mathematical Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong Uninversity, § Carnegie Mellon University, ♢ Fundan University {xiahanchen, chenbaoyou}@sais.org.cn
arxiv-2601-11214.description: Abstract We present T ⋆ , a simple TraceRL -based training curriculum for progressive block-size scaling in masked diffusion language models (MDMs). Starting from an AR-initialized small-block MDM, T ⋆ transitions smoothly to larger blocks, enabling higher-parallelism decoding with minimal performance degradation on math reasoning benchmarks.

pmc-10660044.title: An overview of image-based phenotyping as an adaptive 4.0 technology for studying plant abiotic stress: A bibliometric and literature review
pmc-10660044.creator: Muhammad Fuad Anshori, Andi Dirpan, Trias Sitaresmi, Riccardo Rossi, Muh Farid, Aris Hairmansis, Bambang Sapta Purwoko, Willy Bayuardi Suwarno, Yudhistira Nugraha
pmc-10660044.description: Improving the tolerance of crop species to abiotic stresses that limit plant growth and productivity is essential for mitigating the emerging problems of global warming. In this context, imaged data analysis represents an effective method in the 4.0 technology era, where this method has the non-destructive and recursive characterization of plant phenotypic traits as selection criteria.

pmc-11466416.title: The impact of community based interventions for the prevention and control of soil-transmitted helminths: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11466416.creator: Sommy C. Ugwu, Michael O. Muoka, Clara MacLeod, Sarah Bick, Oliver Cumming, Laura Braun, Humayun Kabir, Khadime Sylla, Khadime Sylla
pmc-11466416.description: Soil-transmitted helminths (STHs) are among the most common human infections worldwide and a major cause of morbidity. They are caused by different species of parasitic worms and transmitted by eggs released in faeces or when hookworm larvae penetrate the skin. The main control strategy in endemic regions is periodic treatment with deworming medication.

pmc-12496290.title: Three-torsion subgroups and wild conductor exponents of plane quartics
pmc-12496290.creator: Elvira Lupoian, James Rawson
pmc-12496290.description: In this paper we give an algorithm to find the 3-torsion subgroup of the Jacobian of a smooth plane quartic curve with a marked rational point. We describe 3-torsion points in terms of cubics which triply intersect the curve, and use this to define a system of equations whose solution set corresponds to the coefficients of these cubics.

pmc-12618243.title: Structural basis for lipid transport at membrane contact sites by the IST2–OSH6 complex
pmc-12618243.creator: Melanie Arndt, Angela Schweri, Raimund Dutzler
pmc-12618243.description: Membrane contact sites are hubs for interorganellar lipid transport within eukaryotic cells. As a principal tether bridging the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the plasma membrane in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the protein IST2 has a major role during lipid transport between both compartments.

pmc-12719557.title: Native GaN/GaOx Heterostructure Platform for Wafer-Scale Integration of High-Performance Complementary Transistors
pmc-12719557.creator: Jinhua Liang, Chi Liu, Yuning Wei, Shun Feng, Yun Sun, Yutaka Ohno, Hui-Ming Cheng, Dong-Ming Sun
pmc-12719557.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The drive for complementary transistors with ultra-steep subthreshold swing (SS) and minimal power consumption has intensified interest in integrating low-dimensional semiconductors with wide-bandgap materials, as silicon scaling approaches its physical limits in the post-Moore era. A central bottleneck, however, lies in dielectric/semiconductor interface engineering: existing strategies based on van der Waals transfer or nonnative dielectric deposition compromise interface quality, wafer-scale uniformity, and process compatibility, preventing practical large-scale integration.

pmc-12827575.title: The association of eight-year trajectories in total, cognitive-affective, and somatic depressive symptoms with incident stroke: a 10-year follow-up study using HRS and ELSA cohorts
pmc-12827575.creator: Haining Zhang, Jiange Chen, Yuntian Ye, Hongyi Wang, Shun Fan, Wei Zhang, An Bao, Huanan Li, Jingui Wang
pmc-12827575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEarlier research has documented an association between depressive symptomatology and heightened stroke risk. However, prior work largely assessed depressive manifestations at isolated time points and failed to differentiate symptom subtypes. This investigation seeks to characterize the longitudinal progression of depressive symptoms via repeated measurement and explore their link to stroke risk by considering total depressive symptoms alongside cognitive-affective and somatic dimensions.MethodsThis prospective cohort study included individuals aged ≥ 45 years from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) in the United States and

pmc-13120068.title: Electrosynthesis of Silver Particles–Polypyrrole on Screen-Printed Carbon Electrodes, with a View to Their Modification with Ki-67 Antibodies
pmc-13120068.creator: Matias Luengo, Loreto A. Hernández, Isabeau D. M. Figueroa, Cindy Peña, Gonzalo Riveros, Eduardo Muñoz
pmc-13120068.description: The development of reliable electrochemical interfaces for biosensor applications requires materials that combine high conductivity, large effective surface area, and suitable platforms for biomolecule immobilization. In this work, a hybrid electrochemical platform based on screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) modified with electropolymerized polypyrrole (PPy) and electrodeposited silver particles (AgPs) is presented for the subsequent immobilization of Ki-67 antibodies.

pmc-13288489.title: Direct access to 2-imidazolines from unactivated alkenes
pmc-13288489.creator: Stefanie Schiele, Ann-Sophie K. Paschke, Giorgia Romiti, Bill Morandi

pmc-13499870.title: Identifying and Comparing Intervention Cost Components in Remote Patient Monitoring: A Scoping Review
pmc-13499870.creator: Anna L. Heilig, Wilbert B. van den Hout, M. Elske van den Akker-van Marle
pmc-13499870.description: Background and ObjectiveRemote patient monitoring has shown promising outcomes, such as improved disease awareness and reduced hospital stay. However, assessing the cost of the remote patient monitoring itself is challenging owing to the lack of standardization and transparency in economic evaluations of remote patient monitoring.
